'''''Vaccinium padifolium''''', commonly known as '''Madeira blueberry''' or '''Uva-de-serra''',<ref name=":0" /> is a Portuguese species of flowering plant.

==Description==
It is a semi-[[evergreen]] scrub to small tree {{Convert|1.5–6|m|ft|frac=2}} tall. New branches are generally reddish and pubescent. The [[leaves]] are {{Convert|2.5–7|cm|frac=2}} long and 1–2.5 cm wide, oblong to elliptic, acute to [[acuminate]], and often flushed dark red in autumn. The [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] is short and pubescent.

The flowers are borne on curved [[pedicels]] in erect, axillary, [[bract]]eate [[raceme]]s. The [[Sepal|calyx]] is {{Convert|3–4|mm|frac=16}}, with five short, broad lobes up to 1.5 mm. The [[Petal|corolla]] is {{Convert|7–10|mm|abbr=on|frac=8}}, globose to campanulate, the lobes very short. There are often five broad rose stripes on the white corolla. The berries are up to {{Convert|12 × 10|mm|abbr=on|frac=8}}, ripening blue-black.

The blue color of the berries is due to [[anthocyanin]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Anthocyanin trisaccharides in blue berries of ''Vaccinium padifolium''|vauthors=Cabrita L, Frøystein NA, Andersen OM| journal=Food Chemistry|volume=69|date= 1 April 2000|pages=33–6|doi=10.1016/S0308-8146(99)00230-7}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
[[File:Vaccinium padifolium bushes on a slope in front of a view towards São Vicente in October 1999..jpg|thumb|Shrubs in [[Madeira]], Portugal]]

The species is [[endemic]] to the islands of [[Madeira Island|Madeira]] and [[Porto Santo]], Portugal. It grows mainly in crevices and exposed slopes and mountain plains. It is very common at elevations between {{convert|800 and 1700|m|abbr=on|sigfig=2}}.

==Uses==
The fruits are used in preserves.
